title: Regular -AR verbs in the preterite
summary: Talk about completed past actions: hablé, hablaste, habló, hablamos, hablasteis, hablaron.
content:
## What the preterite is for

The **pretérito indefinido** describes actions that were **completed** at a specific point in the past:

- *Ayer hablé con mi abuela.* (Yesterday I spoke with my grandmother.)
- *El año pasado viajamos a Perú.* (Last year we travelled to Peru.)

Typical time markers: *ayer*, *anoche*, *la semana pasada*, *el año pasado*, *en 2019*, *hace dos días*.

## The endings

Remove **-ar** and add:

| person | ending | hablar |
|---|---|---|
| yo | **-é** | habl**é** |
| tú | **-aste** | habl**aste** |
| él / ella / usted | **-ó** | habl**ó** |
| nosotros/as | **-amos** | habl**amos** |
| vosotros/as | **-asteis** | habl**asteis** |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **-aron** | habl**aron** |

## Watch the accents

The **yo** and **él/ella/usted** forms carry a written accent on the last syllable: *hablé*, *habló*. Without it the meaning changes:

- *hablo* = I speak (present) vs. *habló* = he/she spoke (past)
- *canto* = I sing vs. *cantó* = he/she sang

## Nosotros looks the same as the present

*Hablamos* is both *we speak* and *we spoke*. Context or a time marker tells you which. *Ayer hablamos* = yesterday we spoke.

## Spelling changes in the yo form

Verbs ending in **-car**, **-gar** and **-zar** change spelling in the **yo** form to keep the sound:

- buscar → bus**qué**
- llegar → lle**gué**
- empezar → empe**cé**

vocabulary.example_meaning: Yesterday I spoke with my grandmother.
You all sang at the party.

vocabulary.example: Ayer María habló con su jefe.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Yesterday María talked to her boss.
Last night you watched the film.

vocabulary.example: La semana pasada viajamos a Sevilla.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Last week we travelled to Seville.
Did you watch the film last night?

quiz.explanation: The yo preterite ending is -é with an accent: 'hablé'.
María = ella, which takes -ó in the preterite. 'Hablo' without the accent is present tense 'I speak'.
Verbs in -gar change g → gu before é in the yo form, to keep the hard g sound: 'llegué'.

quiz.prompt: La semana pasada nosotros ___ a Sevilla.
quiz.explanation: Nosotros takes -amos in both present and preterite; 'la semana pasada' makes it past: 'viajamos'.
hints: Nosotros looks the same in present and preterite.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence means 'I looked for the keys'?
quiz.explanation: -car verbs change c → qu in the yo preterite: 'busqué'. 'Busco' is present, 'buscó' is he/she.
hints: -car verbs: c → qu in the yo form.

listening.meaning: Did you talk to your boss?
Yesterday I worked a lot at home.
listening.note: Yo form: accent on the final é.

listening.meaning: Last night we sang in the bar.
listening.note: Cantamos is present or past; anoche makes it past.

listening.meaning: Where did you all look for the car keys?

listening.text: Mis padres llegaron temprano a la fiesta.
listening.meaning: My parents arrived early at the party.

listening.text: La semana pasada viajé a Madrid con mi hermana.
listening.meaning: Last week I travelled to Madrid with my sister.

listening.text: Anoche Luis y yo miramos una película muy aburrida.
listening.meaning: Last night Luis and I watched a very boring film.

listening.text: Ayer llegué a la oficina a las nueve y hablé con la jefa.
listening.meaning: Yesterday I got to the office at nine and spoke to the boss.
listening.note: New word: la oficina = the office.

Spelling changes in the yo form

conversations.title: Last weekend
conversations.scenario: Lucía and Mateo catch up on Monday morning about what they did at the weekend.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Hola, Mateo. ¿Qué tal el fin de semana?
lines.meaning: Hi, Mateo. How was the weekend?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Genial! El sábado viajé a Toledo con mi hermana.
lines.meaning: Great! On Saturday I travelled to Toledo with my sister.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Nice! Did you (both) visit the cathedral?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí, y después caminamos por el centro y cenamos en un restaurante pequeño.
lines.meaning: Yes, and afterwards we walked around the centre and had dinner in a small restaurant.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: What time did you get home?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Llegamos muy tarde, a la una. ¿Y tú? ¿Qué pasó el domingo?
lines.meaning: We got home very late, at one. And you? What happened on Sunday?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Yo descansé. Por la mañana estudié español y por la tarde escuché música.
lines.meaning: I rested. In the morning I studied Spanish and in the afternoon I listened to music.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Did you finish the preterite exercises?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí, los terminé anoche. ¡Y busqué todas las palabras nuevas en el diccionario!
lines.meaning: Yes, I finished them last night. And I looked up all the new words in the dictionary!

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Very good! I didn't study at all.

bites.title: Finished actions
bites.rule: The preterite is for actions finished at a specific point in the past, usually flagged by ayer, anoche, la semana pasada or el año pasado.
bites.example_meaning: Yesterday I spoke with my grandmother.

bites.title: The accent marks the past
bites.rule: Hablo = I speak; habló = he spoke. One accent on the last syllable makes the verb past. Yo ends in -é, él/ella in -ó.

bites.title: Learn the endings
bites.rule: Drop -ar and add -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron. Tú never takes an extra -s: miraste, not mirastes.
bites.example_meaning: Did you watch the film last night?

bites.title: Yo fixes its spelling
bites.rule: To keep the sound before -é, yo changes spelling: buscar → busqué, llegar → llegué, empezar → empecé. Only yo changes. Buscó and llegó are regular.
bites.example: Llegué tarde y busqué las llaves.
bites.example_meaning: I arrived late and looked for the keys.

sorts.title: Present or past?
sorts.why: The accent on -é/-ó and the -aste ending mark the preterite; -o without an accent and -as are present.

sorts.title: Spelling change in yo?
sorts.why: -car → -qué, -gar → -gué, -zar → -cé in the yo form; other -ar verbs just add -é.

spots.sentence: Ayer María hablo con su jefe.
spots.why: Ella in the past needs the accented -ó; hablo is present 'I speak'.

spots.sentence: Ayer yo hable con mi abuela.
spots.why: The yo preterite ends in an accented -é: hablé.
The tú preterite ends in -aste, with no final s.
-car verbs change c → qu before é: busqué.
-gar verbs add a u before é to keep the hard g: llegué.

spots.sentence: La semana pasada mis primos trabajó mucho.

builds.meaning: Yesterday I spoke with my grandmother.
Did you watch the film last night?

builds.meaning: Last week we travelled to Seville.
